source.title: Zagier–Hoffman's conjectures in positive characteristic
source.authors: Bo-Hae Im, Hojin Kim, Khac Nhuan Le, Tuan Ngo Dac, Lan Huong Pham
source.read: arXiv v2 (10 June 2024), 60 pages, the version whose comment records that the details of proofs were added. Read in the LaTeX source of that version (arXiv e-print of 2205.07165v2, file AMZV_ZagierHoffman_arxiv_v2.tex, sha256 of the source archive 362cf73f69e7a7adc58c10667cf3226004842e3384191bd2b628bc43ca1c29b1), fetched 22 September 2026, together with the open-access published version at doi:10.1017/fmp.2024.18 on Cambridge Core. readSections: 0 Introduction (0.1 Classical setting, 0.2 Function field setting with the conjectures of Zagier–Hoffman type, 0.3 Main results and ingredients of the proofs)
1 Weak and strong Brown's theorems for ACMPL's (1.1 Analogues of power sums, 1.2 A strong version of Brown's theorem for ACMPL's)
4 Applications on AMZV's and Zagier–Hoffman's conjectures in positive characteristic (including the sharp bounds without ACMPL's)

summary: Im, Kim, Le, Ngo Dac and Pham determine the dimensions of the spaces of alternating multiple zeta values in positive characteristic and prove the analogues of Zagier's and Hoffman's conjectures. Over A = F_q[θ] with K = F_q(θ), Thakur's multiple zeta values ζ_A(s) and Harada's alternating values ζ_A(ε; s) span K-vector spaces Z_w and AZ_w in each weight. Their Theorem A computes dim_K AZ_w = s(w) for an explicit Fibonacci-like sequence and exhibits a Hoffman-like basis; their Theorem B proves Thakur's basis conjecture, that the values ζ_A(s) with s_i ≤ q for i < r and s_r < q form a basis of Z_w, and with it Todd's dimension conjecture. The method does not work inside the theory of alternating multiple zeta values, where the available algorithm only produces a generating set that is too large; instead the paper develops the algebraic theory of alternating Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, whose stuffle relations are simpler, proves a strong Brown theorem there with a generating set AS_w of exactly the right size, and establishes a bridge AZ_w = AL_w between the two theories. The linear independence of the proposed basis comes from the Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion applied to dual t-motives, through an improved criterion (their Theorem 2.4) that controls the coefficients of a hypothetical relation, a character-splitting lemma and a Kuan–Lin degree bound. The atlas plans the Carlitz module, its period, Anderson t-motives, Carlitz zeta values and Papanikolas's difference-Galois theory in the roadmap Drinfeld modules, t-motives and characteristic-p special values, and stops at depth one; the classical analogues are planned at PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.9. Nothing plans multiple zeta values in characteristic p, their alternating versions, Carlitz polylogarithms or the ABP criterion. This extraction proposes the same Part II as the extraction of Chang–Chen–Mishiba, which proves Theorem B independently and simultaneously, and asks for the two to be designed together. Reviewed by REV-PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 99 items (1 library, 11 planned, 87 missing). 36 mistakes are confirmed (29 misprints, 6 gaps, 1 error; 1 reaches a stated result, 5 a proof). Theorems A and B stand. The gaps are in proofs and are repaired with the paper's own tools: the congruence behind the strong Brown theorem (E12), the passage between Li- and 𝔏𝔦-relations in Theorem 3.4 (E30, E23), the inclusion S_w ⊂ Z_w in Proposition 4.10 (E31) and the empty case of Proposition 4.11 (E33); Condition (2.1) as stated does not make the sub-tuple series converge, which affects none of the applications (E14). Not formalised.

items.name: The base ring and fields
items.statement: Let F_q be a finite field with q elements, of characteristic p > 0. A = F_q[θ] is the polynomial ring in θ over F_q and A_+ the set of monic polynomials in A; K = F_q(θ) is the fraction field of A, equipped with the rational point ∞; K_∞ is the completion of K at ∞ and C_∞ the completion at ∞ of a fixed algebraic closure K̄ of K. v_∞ is the discrete valuation of K at ∞ normalised by v_∞(θ) = −1, |·|_∞ = q^{−v_∞} the associated absolute value, and the unique valuation of C_∞ extending v_∞ is still written v_∞. F̄_q is the algebraic closure of F_q in K̄. Finally N = {1, 2, …} and Z^{≥0} = {0, 1, 2, …}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.2.1, p. 3 (published: Section 1.2.1)
items.note: Mathlib has polynomial rings over a finite field, rational functions and Laurent series with monic polynomials; the valuation-theoretic package and C_∞ are assumed by the DrinfeldModulesAndTModules roadmap (analytic uniformisation in DM.2) without being constructed.

items.name: Carlitz zeta values
items.statement: For n ∈ N, ζ_A(n) = Σ_{a ∈ A_+} a^{−n} ∈ K_∞ are the Carlitz zeta values, the depth-one case of the multiple values.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.2.1, p. 3 (published: Section 1.2.1)
items.note: DM.0 constructs the Carlitz module, DM.2 its uniformisation and period, and DM.6 requires the explicit Carlitz zeta value and period normalisation.

items.name: Thakur's multiple zeta values
items.statement: For a tuple of positive integers s = (s_1, …, s_r) ∈ N^r, Thakur's multiple zeta value is ζ_A(s) = ζ_A(s_1, …, s_r) := Σ 1/(a_1^{s_1} ⋯ a_r^{s_r}) ∈ K_∞, the sum over all (a_1, …, a_r) ∈ A_+^r with deg a_1 > ⋯ > deg a_r; r is its depth and w(s) = s_1 + ⋯ + s_r its weight, and ζ_A(∅) := 1 (§1.1.3, p. 8, where equivalently ζ_A(s) = Σ_{d≥0} S_d(s)). Carlitz zeta values are exactly the depth-one MZVs, and Thakur [Tha09a] showed that no MZV vanishes. For w ∈ N, Z_w denotes the K-vector space spanned by the MZVs of weight w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.2.1, p. 3, and Section 1.1.3, p. 8 (published: Sections 1.2.1 and 2.1.3)
items.note: The same object as in PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23; the two papers prove the same theorem independently and should be routed together.

items.name: Alternating multiple zeta values
items.statement: Following Harada, for s = (s_1, …, s_r) ∈ N^r and ε = (ε_1, …, ε_r) ∈ (F_q^×)^r one sets ζ_A(ε; s) = Σ ε_1^{deg a_1} ⋯ ε_r^{deg a_r} / (a_1^{s_1} ⋯ a_r^{s_r}) ∈ K_∞, the sum over (a_1, …, a_r) ∈ A_+^r with deg a_1 > ⋯ > deg a_r, with ζ_A(∅; ∅) = 1; AZ_w denotes the K-span of the AMZVs of weight w. Harada extended non-vanishing, shuffle relations, the period interpretation and linear independence to these values.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.2.2, p. 4 (published: Section 1.2.2)
items.note: The alternating values are the new object of this paper; they are not in the atlas, and not in the companion paper of Chang, Chen and Mishiba either.

items.name: Carlitz multiple polylogarithms and their alternating version
items.statement: Put ℓ_0 := 1 and ℓ_d := ∏_{i=1}^d (θ − θ^{q^i}) for d ∈ N. For s = (s_1, …, s_n) ∈ N^n, the Carlitz multiple polylogarithm (CMPL) is Li(s) := Σ_{d≥0} Si_d(s) = Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_n ≥ 0} 1/(ℓ_{d_1}^{s_1} ⋯ ℓ_{d_n}^{s_n}) ∈ K_∞, with Li(∅) := 1. For an array (ε; s) with ε = (ε_1, …, ε_n) ∈ (F_q^×)^n, the alternating Carlitz multiple polylogarithm (ACMPL) is Li(ε; s) := Σ_{d≥0} Si_d(ε; s) = Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_n ≥ 0} ε_1^{d_1} ⋯ ε_n^{d_n}/(ℓ_{d_1}^{s_1} ⋯ ℓ_{d_n}^{s_n}) ∈ K_∞, with Li(∅; ∅) := 1. Its depth is n, its weight w(s) = s_1 + ⋯ + s_n and its character χ(ε) = ε_1 ⋯ ε_n. For w ∈ N, AL_w denotes the K-vector space spanned by the ACMPLs of weight w. When all ε_i = 1 the ACMPL is the CMPL Li(s).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.3.2, p. 5, and Sections 1.1.3–1.1.4, pp. 8–9 (published: Sections 1.3.2 and 2.1.3–2.1.4)
items.note: The objects the whole proof is carried out with; DM.8 plans Carlitz logarithms, not polylogarithms, and nothing plans the alternating versions.

items.name: Power sums for both realisations
items.statement: For d ∈ Z and s = (s_1, …, s_n) ∈ N^n: S_d(s) := Σ 1/(a_1^{s_1} ⋯ a_n^{s_n}) over a_1, …, a_n ∈ A_+ with d = deg a_1 > ⋯ > deg a_n ≥ 0, and S_{<d}(s) the same sum over d > deg a_1 > ⋯ > deg a_n ≥ 0; Si_d(s) := Σ_{d = d_1 > ⋯ > d_n ≥ 0} 1/(ℓ_{d_1}^{s_1} ⋯ ℓ_{d_n}^{s_n}) and Si_{<d}(s) := Σ_{d > d_1 > ⋯ > d_n ≥ 0} 1/(ℓ_{d_1}^{s_1} ⋯ ℓ_{d_n}^{s_n}); all four lie in K, and ζ_A(s) = Σ_{d≥0} S_d(s), Li(s) = Σ_{d≥0} Si_d(s). For an array (ε; s) = (ε_1 … ε_n; s_1 … s_n), S_d(ε; s) and S_{<d}(ε; s) are the same sums with numerator ε_1^{deg a_1} ⋯ ε_n^{deg a_n}, and Si_d(ε; s), Si_{<d}(ε; s) the same sums with numerator ε_1^{d_1} ⋯ ε_n^{d_n}; they lie in K. One has Si_d(ε; s) = ε^d Si_d(s) in depth one, Si_d(1, …, 1; s_1, …, s_n) = Si_d(s_1, …, s_n), Si_{<d}(1, …, 1; s_1, …, s_n) = Si_{<d}(s_1, …, s_n), and Si_d(ε; s) = Si_d(ε_1; s_1) Si_{<d}(ε_−; s_−), where ε_− = (ε_2, …, ε_n) and s_− = (s_2, …, s_n).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Sections 1.1.3 and 1.1.4, pp. 8–9 (published: Sections 2.1.3 and 2.1.4)
items.note: The two families of truncated sums whose product formulae drive the algebraic part.

items.name: Zagier's conjecture
items.statement: For k ∈ N let Z_k be the Q-vector space spanned by the multiple zeta values ζ(n_1, …, n_r) = Σ_{0<k_1<⋯<k_r} 1/(k_1^{n_1} ⋯ k_r^{n_r}) (n_i ≥ 1, n_r ≥ 2) of weight n_1 + ⋯ + n_r = k. Define d_0 = 1, d_1 = 0, d_2 = 1 and d_k = d_{k−2} + d_{k−3} for k ≥ 3. Then dim_Q Z_k = d_k for all k ∈ N.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Conjecture 0.1, p. 2 (published: Conjecture 1.1)
items.note: PS.9 plans classical multiple zeta values with shuffle and stuffle, regularisation, the mixed-Tate category and 'selected motivic basis/spanning and numerical spanning results' — that is, exactly Zagier, Hoffman, Terasoma–Deligne–Goncharov and Brown. The alternating classical case is of the same kind and belongs there too.

items.name: Zagier's conjecture in positive characteristic
items.statement: With d(0) = 1, d(w) = 2^{w−1} for 1 ≤ w ≤ q − 1, d(q) = 2^{q−1} − 1 and d(w) = Σ_{i=1}^q d(w−i) for w > q, one has dim_K Z_w = d(w) for every w ∈ N.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Conjecture 0.6, p. 3 (published: Conjecture 1.6)
items.note: The same conjecture appears in PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23 as its Conjecture 1.2.2; the two papers prove it independently.

items.name: Hoffman's conjecture in positive characteristic
items.statement: A K-basis of Z_w is given by the set T_w of ζ_A(s_1, …, s_r) of weight w with s_i ≤ q for 1 ≤ i < r and s_r < q.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Conjecture 0.7, p. 4 (published: Conjecture 1.7); the set T_w is defined in Section 0.2.1, p. 3
items.note: Thakur's basis conjecture, the same statement as Conjecture 1.2.3 of PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23.

items.name: Ngo Dac's Brown-type theorem in positive characteristic ([ND21, Theorem A])
items.statement: [ND21, Theorem A] For every w ∈ N, every MZV of weight w is a K-linear combination of MZVs in T_w; in particular dim_K Z_w ≤ d(w). (The paper quotes only the inequality, on pp. 4 and 54, and proves it from the Chen–Thakur shuffle relations and Todd's operators. The proof of Theorem B on p. 54 invokes it as 'the sharp upper bound'; to conclude that T_w is a basis it needs the spanning form, because T_w ⊂ Z_w and |T_w| = d(w).)
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.2.1, p. 4, and Section 4.3.1, p. 54 (published: Sections 1.2.1 and 5.3.1), quoting [ND21, Theorem A]
items.note: The state of the art this paper completes, and the source of the algebraic method it generalises.

items.name: Dimensions and a Hoffman-like basis for alternating multiple zeta values
items.statement: Define s(w) = (q − 1)q^{w−1} for 1 ≤ w < q, s(q) = (q − 1)(q^{q−1} − 1), and s(w) = (q − 1)Σ_{i=1}^{q−1} s(w−i) + s(w−q) for w > q. Then dim_K AZ_w = s(w) for every w ∈ N, and an explicit Hoffman-like basis of AZ_w is exhibited.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem A, p. 4 (published: Theorem A)
items.note: The main theorem for alternating values, and the harder of the two; it has no counterpart in the companion paper.

items.name: Zagier–Hoffman's conjectures in positive characteristic
items.statement: For every w ∈ N, T_w is a K-basis of Z_w; in particular dim_K Z_w = d(w).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem B, p. 5 (published: Theorem B)
items.note: Thakur's basis conjecture and Todd's dimension conjecture. The same theorem is proved independently in PAPER-CHANG-CHEN-MISHIBA-23 (its Theorem 1.2.4); the authors record the simultaneity in the remark closing the introduction.

items.name: Strategy: passing through alternating Carlitz multiple polylogarithms
items.statement: Overview of the proof strategy (§0.3.2). Working with AMZVs alone and following [ND21, §2–3] gives only a weak Brown theorem: a generating set of AZ_w too large to be a basis, because the algorithm moves forward without control of the coefficients. The paper instead develops the algebraic theory of ACMPLs by stuffle relations and obtains a weak Brown theorem for AL_w with the same generating set as for AMZVs, hence AL_w = AZ_w (Theorem 4.9). It then uses three new ingredients. (1) A Hoffman-like system of bases AS_w of AL_w satisfying the constraints of Theorem 2.4. (2) A strong Brown theorem for ACMPLs (Theorem 1.11), proved by showing that a transition matrix is invertible. (3) The K-linear independence of the ACMPLs in AS_w (Theorem 3.4). For (3), one considers relations between the ACMPLs in AS_w and π̃^w and applies the ABP criterion to reduce to a system of σ-linear equations. For q − 1 | w this system has a unique solution up to a scalar, and the strong Brown theorem shows that the coefficient of π̃^w in the resulting unique relation is nonzero. This determines all K-linear relations between ACMPLs (Theorem 3.6).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.3.2, pp. 5–6 (published: Section 1.3.2)
items.note: The three new ingredients the authors isolate: the basis AS_w, the strong Brown theorem, and the improved linear-independence criterion of Theorem 2.4.

items.name: Tuples, arrays and their orders
items.statement: A tuple is s = (s_1, …, s_n) ∈ N^n, with depth(s) = n and weight w(s) = s_1 + ⋯ + s_n; if s is nonempty, s_− := (s_2, …, s_n). For tuples s, t of positive integers, set s_i = 0 for i > depth(s) (likewise for t), and write s ≤ t if s_1 + ⋯ + s_i ≤ t_1 + ⋯ + t_i for all i ∈ N and w(s) = w(t); this is a partial order. For i ∈ N, T_i(s) := (s_1 + ⋯ + s_i, s_{i+1}, …, s_n). For s ∈ N^n let 0 ≤ i ≤ n be the largest integer with s_j ≤ q for all 1 ≤ j ≤ i, and let Init(s) := (s_1, …, s_i) (empty if s_1 > q). Initial tuples are compared in the lexicographic order ≼ (≺, ≽, ≻). For s ∈ N^n and ε = (ε_1, …, ε_n) ∈ (F_q^×)^n, the array (ε; s) = (ε_1 … ε_n; s_1 … s_n) has depth n, weight w(s) and character χ(ε) = ε_1 ⋯ ε_n; ε_− := (ε_2, …, ε_n). Write (ε; s) ≤ (ϵ; t) if (1) χ(ε) = χ(ϵ), (2) w(s) = w(t) and (3) s_1 + ⋯ + s_i ≤ t_1 + ⋯ + t_i for all i ∈ N. This is only a preorder on arrays.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Sections 1.1.1 and 1.1.2, pp. 7–8 (published: Sections 2.1.1 and 2.1.2)
items.note: The combinatorial framework; the order on arrays is only a preorder, which is why the arguments track characters separately.

items.name: Depth is reversed by the order
items.statement: If (ε; s) ≤ (e; t) as arrays then depth(s) ≥ depth(t).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Remark 1.1, p. 8 (published: Remark 2.1)
items.note: The elementary consequence of the partial-sum inequalities used throughout the induction.

items.name: The two power sums agree in the Thakur range
items.statement: For an array with s_i ≤ q for all i, S_d(ε; s) = 𝔖_d(ε; s) for all d ∈ Z, and therefore ζ_A(ε; s) = Li(ε; s).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Lemma 1.2, p. 9, proof p. 10 (published: Lemma 2.2)
items.note: Carlitz's identity in the alternating setting; it is what lets the two theories be compared index by index.

items.name: Product formulae for the ACMPL power sums (Proposition 1.3, Parts 1 and 2)
items.statement: Let (ε; s) and (ϵ; t) be two arrays. (1) There exist f_i ∈ F_q and arrays (μ_i; u_i) with (μ_i; u_i) ≤ (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) and depth(u_i) ≤ depth(s) + depth(t) for all i such that Si_d(ε; s) Si_d(ϵ; t) = Σ_i f_i Si_d(μ_i; u_i) for all d ∈ Z. (2) There exist f'_i ∈ F_q and arrays (μ'_i; u'_i) with (μ'_i; u'_i) ≤ (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) and depth(u'_i) ≤ depth(s) + depth(t) for all i such that Si_{<d}(ε; s) Si_{<d}(ϵ; t) = Σ_i f'_i Si_{<d}(μ'_i; u'_i) for all d ∈ Z.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 1.3 (1)–(2), pp. 10–11, proof pp. 11–13 (published: Proposition 2.3 (1)–(2))
items.note: The stuffle relations for ACMPLs, which are simpler than the shuffle relations for AMZVs — the technical reason the paper works with ACMPLs. Note: read with the paper's definition of character, Proposition 1.3 shows only that the span of the trivial-character ACMPLs is closed under products; that the CMPL span is an algebra follows from the proof or from [ND21, Proposition 2.1] (E6).

items.name: Binary and fixed relations
items.statement: A binary relation is an identity Σ_i a_i 𝔖_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i 𝔖_{d+1}(e_i; t_i) = 0 valid for all d ∈ Z, with a_i, b_i ∈ K and all arrays of the same weight; it is a fixed relation when all b_i vanish.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Definition 1.4, p. 14 (published: Definition 2.4)
items.note: The calculus of relations between truncated sums at consecutive degrees, the same device as in the companion paper's appendix.

items.name: The iterated operator B*_{Σ,V} on a binary relation (Lemma 1.5)
items.statement: Let R ∈ 𝔅ℜ_w be a binary relation R(d): Σ_i a_i Si_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i Si_{d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i) = 0 (a_i, b_i ∈ K, all arrays of weight w), and write ϵ_i = (ϵ_{i1}, ϵ_{i−}), t_i = (t_{i1}, t_{i−}). Let (Σ; V) = (σ_1 … σ_n; v_1 … v_n) be an array. Then B*_{Σ,V}(R) := B*_{σ_1,v_1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ B*_{σ_n,v_n}(R) is of the form Σ_i a_i Si_d(Σ, ε_i; V, s_i) + Σ_i b_i Si_d(Σ, ϵ_i; V, t_i) + Σ_i b_i Si_d(σ_1, …, σ_{n−1}, σ_n ϵ_{i1}, ϵ_{i−}; v_1, …, v_{n−1}, v_n + t_{i1}, t_{i−}) = 0 (for all d ∈ Z; a fixed relation).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Lemma 1.5, p. 15 (published: Lemma 2.5)
items.note: The two operators that generate new relations from old, the engine of the rewriting.

items.name: Decomposition of an ACMPL along its initial tuple (Proposition 1.7, Part 1)
items.statement: Let (ε; s) = (ε_1 … ε_n; s_1 … s_n) be an array such that Init(s) = (s_1, …, s_{k−1}) for some 1 ≤ k ≤ n (so s_k > q), and let ε ∈ F_q^×. Then Li(ε; s) = −Li(ε'; s') [type 1] + Σ_i b_i Li(ϵ'_i; t'_i) [type 2] + Σ_i c_i Li(μ_i; u_i) [type 3], where b_i, c_i ∈ A are divisible by D_1 = θ^q − θ and, for all i: (a) every array (ϵ; t) appearing on the right-hand side satisfies depth(t) ≥ depth(s) and T_k(t) ≤ T_k(s); (b) the type-1 array is (ε'; s') = (ε_1, …, ε_{k−1}, ε, ε^{−1}ε_k, ε_{k+1}, …, ε_n; s_1, …, s_{k−1}, q, s_k − q, s_{k+1}, …, s_n), and s'_1 + ⋯ + s'_ℓ < s_1 + ⋯ + s_ℓ for all k ≤ ℓ ≤ n; (c) every type-2 array (ϵ'; t') satisfies t'_1 + ⋯ + t'_ℓ < s_1 + ⋯ + s_ℓ for all k ≤ ℓ ≤ n; (d) every type-3 array (μ; u) satisfies Init(s) ≺ Init(u).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 1.7, Part 1), p. 17, proof pp. 18–20 (published: Proposition 2.7 (1))
items.note: The step that strictly increases the initial tuple, which makes the algorithm terminate.

items.name: k-admissible tuples
items.statement: A tuple s is k-admissible if s_1, …, s_k ≤ q and s is not of the form (s_1, …, s_r) with r ≤ k, s_1, …, s_{r−1} ≤ q and s_r = q (with s_i = 0 for i > depth(s)); the empty array is k-admissible, and an array is k-admissible when its tuple is.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Definition 1.8, p. 21 (published: Definition 2.8); recalled from [30, Definition 3.1] = T. Ngo Dac, Ann. of Math. (2) 194 (2021)
items.note: The measure of progress for the rewriting algorithm.

items.name: Reduction to k-admissible arrays
items.statement: For every k ∈ N and every array, Li(ε; s) is a K-linear combination of Li(e; t) of the same weight with t k-admissible.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 1.9, p. 21, proof pp. 22–23 (published: Proposition 2.9)
items.note: The termination statement for the rewriting, proved by the strictly increasing sequence of initial tuples.

items.name: Weak Brown theorem for ACMPLs
items.statement: For every w ∈ N, the set AT_w of ACMPLs Li(ε; s) = Li(ε_1 … ε_n; s_1 … s_n) of weight w with s_1, …, s_{n−1} ≤ q and s_n < q (ε ∈ (F_q^×)^n arbitrary) generates the K-vector space AL_w spanned by all ACMPLs of weight w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 1.10, p. 24 (published: Proposition 2.10)
items.note: The generating set is too large to be a basis — this is precisely the weakness of the earlier method that the paper overcomes.

items.name: The sets J_w, J'_w, the Hoffman-like set AS_w and its cardinality s(w)
items.statement: J_w is the set of positive tuples s = (s_1, …, s_n) of weight w with s_1, …, s_{n−1} ≤ q and s_n < q, and J'_w is the set of positive tuples of weight w with q ∤ s_i for all i. The map ι : J'_w → J_w, which writes s_i = h_i q + r_i (0 < r_i < q, h_i ≥ 0) and sends s to (q^{h_1}, r_1, …, q^{h_n}, r_n) (q^{h} = h copies of q), is a bijection. AS_w is the set of ACMPLs Li(ε; s) with s ∈ J'_w and ε ∈ (F_q^×)^{depth s} arbitrary. Let AJ_w be the set of arrays (ε; s) of weight w with q ∤ s_i for all i, and AJ^1_w the set of arrays of weight w with s_1, …, s_{n−1} ≤ q, s_n < q and ε_i = 1 whenever s_i = q. The map φ : AJ_w → AJ^1_w, which writes s_i = (h_i − 1)q + r_i and replaces the column (ε_i; s_i) by h_i − 1 columns (1; q) followed by (ε_i; r_i), is a bijection. Hence s(w) := |AS_w| = |AJ_w| = |AJ^1_w|, and s(w) = (q − 1)q^{w−1} for 1 ≤ w < q, s(q) = (q − 1)(q^{q−1} − 1), and s(w) = (q − 1)Σ_{i=1}^{q−1} s(w − i) + s(w − q) for w > q (the s(w) of Theorem A). |AS_w| < |AT_w| unless q = 2 or w ≤ q, where they are equal.
items.note: The Hoffman-like basis: the first of the three new ingredients, and the one the transcendence method dictates.

items.name: Strong Brown theorem for ACMPLs
items.statement: The set AS_w generates AL_w; in particular dim_K AL_w ≤ s(w).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 1.11, p. 25 (published: Theorem 2.11)
items.note: The second new ingredient: a generating set of the right size, obtained by going backwards through the rewriting with control on the coefficients. Correction: the proof's congruence modulo D_1 must be established by running Proposition 1.7 at every step with matching characters and A-integral coefficients (E12).

items.name: Effective dual t-motives
items.statement: An effective dual t-motive is a K̄[t, σ]-module M' which is free and finitely generated over K̄[t] and satisfies (t − θ)^ℓ (M'/σM') = 0 for ℓ ≫ 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Definition 2.1, p. 26 (published: Definition 3.1)
items.note: DM.8 constructs the neutral Tannakian category of rigid analytically trivial motives of Papanikolas's theorem, whose objects are the effective dual t-motives defined here (left K̄[t, σ]-modules free of finite rank over K̄[t]); DM.4 plans Anderson t-modules and effective t-motives in the τ-form, of which these are the σ-duals.

items.name: The Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas criterion
items.statement: Let Φ ∈ Mat_ℓ(K̄[t]) with det Φ = c(t − θ)^s for some c ∈ K̄^× and s ≥ 0, let ψ ∈ Mat_{ℓ×1}(E) satisfy ψ^{(−1)} = Φψ, and let ρ ∈ Mat_{1×ℓ}(K̄) satisfy ρψ(θ) = 0. Then there is P ∈ Mat_{1×ℓ}(K̄[t]) with Pψ = 0 and P(θ) = ρ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 2.2, p. 26 (published: Theorem 3.2), quoting [ABP04, Theorem 3.1.1]
items.note: The same criterion the companion paper uses; it belongs inside DM.8, which plans the Papanikolas theory built on it.

items.name: The dual t-motives M_{s,Q}, their rigid analytic trivializations Ψ_{s,Q} and Chang's series 𝔏(s;Q) (general case)
items.statement: Let s = (s_1,…,s_r) ∈ ℕ^r be a tuple of positive integers and Q = (Q_1,…,Q_r) ∈ K̄[t]^r satisfy Condition (2.1): (‖Q_1‖_∞/|θ|_∞^{qs_1/(q−1)})^{q^{i_1}} ⋯ (‖Q_r‖_∞/|θ|_∞^{qs_r/(q−1)})^{q^{i_r}} → 0 as 0 ≤ i_r < ⋯ < i_1 and i_1 → ∞ (‖·‖_∞ the Gauss norm). The dual t-motive M_{s,Q} is given by the lower bidiagonal matrix Φ_{s,Q} ∈ Mat_{r+1}(K̄[t]). Its diagonal entries are (Φ_{s,Q})_{k+1,k+1} = (t−θ)^{s_{k+1}+⋯+s_r} for 0 ≤ k ≤ r, so the last one is 1. Its subdiagonal entries are (Φ_{s,Q})_{k+1,k} = Q_k^{(−1)}(t−θ)^{s_k+⋯+s_r} for 1 ≤ k ≤ r, and all other entries are 0. M'_{s,Q} is given by the upper-left r×r submatrix Φ'_{s,Q}. With Ω as in §2.2.1, Chang's series is (2.2) 𝔏(s;Q) = 𝔏(s_1,…,s_r;Q_1,…,Q_r) := Σ_{i_1>⋯>i_r≥0} (Ω^{s_r}Q_r)^{(i_r)} ⋯ (Ω^{s_1}Q_1)^{(i_1)}. The matrix Ψ_{s,Q} ∈ GL_{r+1}(𝕋) is lower triangular, with (Ψ_{s,Q})_{k+1,j} = 𝔏(s_j,…,s_k;Q_j,…,Q_k)·Ω^{s_{k+1}+⋯+s_r} for 1 ≤ j ≤ k+1 ≤ r+1 (with 𝔏(∅) = 1). Its last row is (𝔏(s_1,…,s_r;Q_1,…,Q_r), 𝔏(s_2,…,s_r;Q_2,…,Q_r), …, 𝔏(s_r;Q_r), 1). It satisfies Ψ_{s,Q}^{(−1)} = Φ_{s,Q}Ψ_{s,Q}, so it is a rigid analytic trivialization of M_{s,Q}, and its upper-left r×r submatrix Ψ'_{s,Q} is one of M'_{s,Q}.
items.note: The period interpretation, due to Anderson–Thakur and Chang in the non-alternating case and extended by Harada; it is the bridge between the analytic values and the difference equations. Correction: Condition (2.1) on the whole tuple does not make the sub-tuple series converge; the construction needs the termwise bound (E14).

items.name: K-linear and K̄-linear independence agree
items.statement: Let s_i ∈ ℕ^{r_i} and Q_i ∈ K̄[t]^{r_i} satisfy Condition (2.1) for 1 ≤ i ≤ m, and suppose that all the tuples s_i have the same weight w. Then 𝔏(s_1;Q_1)(θ), …, 𝔏(s_m;Q_m)(θ) are K-linearly independent if and only if they are K̄-linearly independent.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 2.3, p. 28 (published: Proposition 3.3), via [Cha14, Definition 3.4.1 and Proposition 4.3.1]
items.note: The descent of linear independence from K̄ to K, the analogue of Chang's theorem in the companion paper.

items.name: The linear-independence criterion
items.statement: Setup (§2.3.1). Let w ∈ ℕ and let {(s_i;Q_i)}_{1≤i≤n} be pairs satisfying Condition (2.1), each s_i of weight w. Write s_i = (s_{i1},…,s_{iℓ_i}) ∈ ℕ^{ℓ_i} and Q_i = (Q_{i1},…,Q_{iℓ_i}) (printed '∈ (F_q^×)^{ℓ_i}'; see the source issue), so that s_{i1}+⋯+s_{iℓ_i} = w. Put I(s_i;Q_i) := {∅, (s_{i1};Q_{i1}), …, (s_{i1},…,s_{i(ℓ_i−1)};Q_{i1},…,Q_{i(ℓ_i−1)})} and I := ∪_i I(s_i;Q_i). Theorem 2.4. Suppose further: (LW) for every weight w' < w, the values 𝔏(t;Q)(θ) with (t;Q) ∈ I and w(t) = w' are K-linearly independent (in particular each 𝔏(t;Q)(θ) is nonzero); (LD) there exist a ∈ A and a_i ∈ A (1 ≤ i ≤ n), not all zero, with a + Σ_{i=1}^n a_i𝔏(s_i;Q_i)(θ) = 0. For (t;Q) ∈ I set (2.8) f_{t;Q} := Σ_i a_i(t)𝔏(s_{i(k+1)},…,s_{iℓ_i};Q_{i(k+1)},…,Q_{iℓ_i}), where a_i(t) := a_i|_{θ=t} ∈ F_q[t] and the sum runs over the indices i with (t;Q) = (s_{i1},…,s_{ik};Q_{i1},…,Q_{ik}) for some 0 ≤ k ≤ ℓ_i − 1. Then f_{t;Q}(θ) ∈ K for all (t;Q) ∈ I.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 2.4, pp. 29–30, with the setup of §2.3.1 (p. 29) and Eq. (2.8) (published: Theorem 3.4, §3.3.1, Eq. (3.8)); proof pp. 30–33
items.note: The third new ingredient: an improvement of Theorem B of Ngo Dac in two directions, which is what makes the induction on weights work for all weights. Correction: Q_i ranges over K̄[t], as the applications require (E16).

items.name: Roots of unity give independent elements
items.statement: For distinct ε_i ∈ F_q^× and γ_i ∈ F̄_q a (q − 1)-st root of ε_i, the γ_i are F_q-linearly independent.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Lemma 3.1, pp. 33–34 (published: Lemma 4.1)
items.note: The elementary fact that separates the characters in the alternating setting.

items.name: Relations split by character
items.statement: Let Li(ε_i;s_i) ∈ AL_w (ACMPLs of weight w) and a_i ∈ K satisfy Σ_i a_i𝔏i(s_i;ε_i)(θ) = 0, where 𝔏i(s;ε) is the series (2.6). For ε ∈ F_q^× let I(ε) := {i : χ(ε_i) = ε} be the set of indices whose character equals ε. Then Σ_{i∈I(ε)} a_i𝔏i(s_i;ε_i)(θ) = 0 for every ε ∈ F_q^×.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Lemma 3.2, p. 34 (published: Lemma 4.2)
items.note: Reduces any relation to one within a single character class, which is why the character is part of the order on arrays.

items.name: The Kuan–Lin degree bound
items.statement: Let m ∈ N, ε ∈ F_q^×, δ ∈ K̄[t] and F(t, θ) ∈ F̄_q[t, θ] (respectively F_q[t, θ]) satisfy εδ = δ^{(−1)}(t − θ)^m + F^{(−1)}(t, θ). Then δ ∈ F̄_q[t, θ] (respectively F_q[t, θ]) and deg_θ δ ≤ max{qm/(q − 1), deg_θ F(t, θ)/q}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Lemma 3.3, p. 34, proof pp. 34–35 (published: Lemma 4.3)
items.note: The rationality and degree bound for the solutions of the twisted equations, the analogue of the companion paper's Lemmas 4.2.2 and 4.2.3.

items.name: All linear relations between ACMPL values
items.statement: Let w ∈ N and let J'_w be the set of tuples s = (s_1, …, s_n) ∈ N^n of weight w with q ∤ s_i for all i. For an array (ε; s) with s = (s_1, …, s_r), ε = (ε_1, …, ε_r) ∈ (F_q^×)^r put 𝔏𝔦(s; ε)(θ) = γ_1 ⋯ γ_r Li(ε; s)/π̃^{w(s)}, where γ_j ∈ F̄_q is the fixed (q − 1)-th root of ε_j (Eq. (2.7)). Suppose that a + Σ_i a_i 𝔏𝔦(s_i; ε_i)(θ) = 0 is a non-trivial relation with a, a_i ∈ K, the sum running over (distinct) arrays (ε_i; s_i) with s_i ∈ J'_w. Then q − 1 | w and a ≠ 0. Further, if q − 1 | w, there is a unique relation 1 + Σ_i a_i 𝔏𝔦(s_i; ε_i)(θ) = 0 with a_i ∈ K and s_i ∈ J'_w; and for the indices (s_i; ε_i) with non-zero coefficient a_i one has ε_i = (1, …, 1). In particular, the ACMPLs in AS_w are linearly independent over K.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 3.4, p. 35 (published: Theorem 4.4); proof in §3.3, pp. 36–42 (published: §4.3)
items.note: The transcendental heart: it needs the full strength of the strong Brown theorem, as the authors emphasise. Correction: the final step and the 'in particular' clause need that the algebra of §1 preserves characters, or Proposition 2.3 (E30, E23).

items.name: The Hoffman-like basis for ACMPLs
items.statement: For every w ∈ N the ACMPLs in AS_w form a basis of AL_w; in particular dim_K AL_w = s(w).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 3.6, p. 36 (published: Theorem 4.6)
items.note: The combination of the strong Brown theorem (upper bound) with the relation theorem (lower bound).

items.name: Products of depth-one power sums in low weight
items.statement: Let s, t ∈ N with s + t ≤ q and ε, ϵ ∈ F_q^×. Then S_d(ε; s) S_d(ϵ; t) = S_d(εϵ; s + t) for all d ∈ Z (deduced from Harada's formula (4.1)–(4.2): all the coefficients Δ^i_{s,t} vanish).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Remark 4.1, p. 44 (published: Remark 5.1)
items.note: The degenerate case of the shuffle relation, where no correction terms appear.

items.name: Harada's product formulae for the AMZV power sums
items.statement: Let (ε; s) and (ϵ; t) be two arrays. (1) There exist f_i ∈ F_q and arrays (μ_i; u_i) with (μ_i; u_i) ≤ (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) and depth(u_i) ≤ depth(s) + depth(t) for all i such that S_d(ε; s) S_d(ϵ; t) = Σ_i f_i S_d(μ_i; u_i) for all d ∈ Z. (2) There exist f'_i ∈ F_q and arrays (μ'_i; u'_i) with (μ'_i; u'_i) ≤ (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) and depth(u'_i) ≤ depth(s) + depth(t) for all i such that S_{<d}(ε; s) S_{<d}(ϵ; t) = Σ_i f'_i S_{<d}(μ'_i; u'_i) for all d ∈ Z. (3) There exist f''_i ∈ F_q and arrays (μ''_i; u''_i) with (μ''_i; u''_i) ≤ (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) and depth(u''_i) ≤ depth(s) + depth(t) for all i such that S_d(ε; s) S_{<d}(ϵ; t) = Σ_i f''_i S_d(μ''_i; u''_i) for all d ∈ Z. (Here (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) = (εϵ; s + t) componentwise after padding with ε_i = 1, s_i = 0, and ≤ is the preorder of §1.1.1, which requires equal weight and equal character.)
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.2, p. 44 (published: Proposition 5.2); cited from Harada [21]
items.note: The shuffle relations of Chen–Thakur in Harada's alternating form; they are more complicated than the stuffle relations for ACMPLs, which is why the ACMPL route is taken.

items.name: The operator B*_{Σ,V} on AMZV binary relations in low weight
items.statement: Let (Σ; V) = (σ_1 … σ_n; v_1 … v_n) be an array and let R ∈ ℜ_w be a binary relation Σ_i a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i S_{d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i) = 0 as in (4.3). Suppose that v_n + t_{i1} ≤ q for all i, where t_i = (t_{i1}, t_{i−}). Then B*_{Σ,V}(R) is the fixed relation Σ_i a_i S_d((Σ, ε_i); (V, s_i)) + Σ_i b_i S_d((Σ, ϵ_i); (V, t_i)) + Σ_i b_i S_d((σ_1, …, σ_{n−1}, σ_n ϵ_{i1}, ϵ_{i−}); (v_1, …, v_{n−1}, v_n + t_{i1}, t_{i−})) = 0 (for all d ∈ Z).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Lemma 4.4, p. 45 (published: Lemma 5.4); proof pp. 45–46
items.note: The algebraic theory for AMZVs, following Ngo Dac's method; it gives only the weak Brown theorem below.

items.name: Weak Brown theorem for AMZVs
items.statement: The set of AMZVs ζ_A(ε; s) of weight w with s_1, …, s_{n−1} ≤ q and s_n < q — the same index set AT_w as for ACMPLs — generates AZ_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.8, p. 54 (published: Proposition 5.8)
items.note: The generating set coincides with the one for ACMPLs, which is what makes the bridge possible.

items.name: The bridge between AMZVs and ACMPLs
items.statement: The K-vector space AZ_w of AMZVs of weight w and the K-vector space AL_w of ACMPLs of weight w are equal.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 4.9, p. 54 (published: Theorem 5.9)
items.note: The key result of the paper: it transports the basis theorem for ACMPLs to the alternating multiple zeta values, giving Theorem A.

items.name: The lower bound for multiple zeta values
items.statement: For all w ∈ N we have dim_K Z_w ≥ d(w).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.10, p. 54, proof pp. 54–55 (published: Proposition 5.10)
items.note: The proof restricts the ACMPL basis to the non-alternating indices and uses the bridge. Correction: S_w ⊂ Z_w follows from the trivial-character version of Proposition 1.10 with Lemma 1.2, not from Theorem 4.9 (E31).

items.name: Sharp upper bound for AMZVs in weights w ≤ 2q − 2 without ACMPLs
items.statement: Let w ≤ 2q − 2. Then dim_K AZ_w ≤ s(w).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.11, p. 55, proof pp. 55–57 (published: Proposition 5.11)
items.note: The record of what the direct approach achieves and where it stops, which is the best justification for the ACMPL detour. Correction: the proof's formula (*) fails for U = ∅, which needs the corrected relation (E33).

items.name: Hoffman's conjecture
items.statement: For k ∈ N, the Q-vector space Z_k spanned by the MZVs of weight k has as a basis the MZVs ζ(n_1, …, n_r) of weight k with all n_i ∈ {2, 3}. (Stated in the paper as 'Z_k is generated by the basis consisting of MZV's of weight k of the form ζ(n_1, …, n_r) with n_i ∈ {2, 3}'.)
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Conjecture 0.2, p. 2 (published: Conjecture 1.2)
items.note: Split out of the bundled item PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/7. A conjecture, and still open: Brown's Theorem 0.4 gives the spanning half. It is context only; the proofs never use it. Planned: PS.9 plans classical multiple zeta values with shuffle and stuffle, regularisation, the mixed-Tate category and 'selected motivic basis/spanning and numerical spanning results', which is where the classical Zagier–Hoffman statements, the Deligne–Goncharov and Terasoma bounds and Brown's theorem belong.

items.name: Upper bound for classical MZVs (Deligne–Goncharov, Terasoma)
items.statement: For k ∈ N, dim_Q Z_k ≤ d_k, where d_0 = 1, d_1 = 0, d_2 = 1 and d_k = d_{k−2} + d_{k−3} for k ≥ 3.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 0.3, p. 2 (published: Theorem 1.3), citing [Ter02] and [DG05]
items.note: Split out of the bundled item PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/7. A cited classical result, proved with mixed Tate motives. Context only; the proofs never use it. Planned: PS.9 plans classical multiple zeta values with shuffle and stuffle, regularisation, the mixed-Tate category and 'selected motivic basis/spanning and numerical spanning results', which is where the classical Zagier–Hoffman statements, the Deligne–Goncharov and Terasoma bounds and Brown's theorem belong.

items.name: Brown's theorem
items.statement: For k ∈ N, the Q-vector space Z_k is generated by the MZVs of weight k of the form ζ(n_1, …, n_r) with n_i ∈ {2, 3}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 0.4, p. 2 (published: Theorem 1.4), citing [Bro12]
items.note: Split out of the bundled item PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/7. A cited classical result. Context only: it is the model for the weak and strong 'Brown theorems' of §1. Planned: PS.9 plans classical multiple zeta values with shuffle and stuffle, regularisation, the mixed-Tate category and 'selected motivic basis/spanning and numerical spanning results', which is where the classical Zagier–Hoffman statements, the Deligne–Goncharov and Terasoma bounds and Brown's theorem belong.

items.name: Upper bound for alternating MZVs (Deligne–Goncharov)
items.statement: For k ∈ N let A_k be the Q-vector space spanned by the alternating MZVs (Euler sums) ζ(ε_1, …, ε_r; n_1, …, n_r) = Σ_{0<k_1<⋯<k_r} ε_1^{k_1} ⋯ ε_r^{k_r}/(k_1^{n_1} ⋯ k_r^{n_r}), with ε_i ∈ {±1}, n_i ∈ N and (n_r, ε_r) ≠ (1, 1), of weight n_1 + ⋯ + n_r = k. Then dim_Q A_k ≤ F_{k+1}, where F_1 = F_2 = 1 and F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n for n ≥ 1.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Theorem 0.5, p. 2 (published: Theorem 1.5), citing [DG05]
items.note: Split out of the bundled item PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/7, with the definition of classical alternating MZVs from p. 2. A cited result. Context only; the proofs never use it. Planned: PS.9 plans classical multiple zeta values with shuffle and stuffle, regularisation, the mixed-Tate category and 'selected motivic basis/spanning and numerical spanning results', which is where the classical Zagier–Hoffman statements, the Deligne–Goncharov and Terasoma bounds and Brown's theorem belong.

items.name: Zagier–Hoffman in small weight ([ND21, Theorem D])
items.statement: [ND21, Theorem D] Let w ∈ N with w ≤ 2q − 2. Then T_w is a K-basis of Z_w; in particular dim_K Z_w = d(w). (The paper states this as 'sharp lower bounds for small weights w ≤ 2q − 2', p. 4, and 'Conjecture 0.7 holds for w ≤ 2q − 2', p. 54.)
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 0.2.1, p. 4, and Section 4.3.1, p. 54 (published: Sections 1.2.1 and 5.3.1), quoting [ND21, Theorem D]
items.note: Split out of the bundled item PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/10. Theorem B generalises it and does not use it. The statement was checked against Ngo Dac's paper (HAL version, p. 4). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Comparison of T_i propagates to larger indices
items.statement: For tuples s, t of positive integers and i ∈ N, if T_i(s) ≤ T_i(t) then T_k(s) ≤ T_k(t) for all k ≥ i.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.1.1, p. 7 (published: Section 2.1.1)
items.note: Stated without proof. It is immediate, because T_i(s) ≤ T_i(t) says exactly that w(s) = w(t) and s_1 + ⋯ + s_m ≤ t_1 + ⋯ + t_m for all m ≥ i (with the zero-padding convention). The conclusions 'T_k(t) ≤ T_k(s)' in Propositions 1.7 and 4.5 rely on this reformulation. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Sum of two arrays
items.statement: For arrays (ε; s) and (ϵ; t), set s_i = 0 and ε_i = 1 for i > depth(s), and t_i = 0 and ϵ_i = 1 for i > depth(t). Then (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) := (εϵ; s + t), where εϵ and s + t are the componentwise product and componentwise sum.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.1.5, p. 10 (published: Section 2.1.5)
items.note: Bounds every array produced by the product formulae (Proposition 1.3) and the operators C, BC (e.g. (1; q − 1) + (Σ; V)); not covered by item /14. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Elementary identities for the power sums Si_d
items.statement: For d ∈ Z: Si_d(ε; s) = ε^d Si_d(s) for a depth-one array; Si_d(1, …, 1; s_1, …, s_n) = Si_d(s_1, …, s_n) and Si_{<d}(1, …, 1; s_1, …, s_n) = Si_{<d}(s_1, …, s_n); Si_d(ε; s) = Si_d(ε_1; s_1) Si_{<d}(ε_−; s_−). Moreover (1.1) Si_d(ε; s) Si_d(ϵ; t) = Si_d(εϵ; s + t) for depth-one arrays, hence (1.2) Si_d(ε; s) Si_d(ϵ; t) = Si_d(εϵ_1, ϵ_−; s + t_1, t_−) for t = (t_1, …, t_n).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.1.4, p. 9 ('One verifies easily the following formulas'), and (1.1)–(1.2) in Section 1.1.5, p. 10 (published: Sections 2.1.4–2.1.5)
items.note: (1.1)/(1.2) are cited in the proofs of Proposition 1.3, Lemma 1.5, Proposition 1.6 and the operator B*. The depth-one case of the factorisation uses the unstated convention Si_{<d}(∅; ∅) = 1. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Mixed product formula Si_d · Si_{<d} (Proposition 1.3, Part 3)
items.statement: Let (ε; s) and (ϵ; t) be two arrays. There exist f''_i ∈ F_q and arrays (μ''_i; u''_i) with (μ''_i; u''_i) ≤ (ε; s) + (ϵ; t) and depth(u''_i) ≤ depth(s) + depth(t) for all i such that Si_d(ε; s) Si_{<d}(ϵ; t) = Σ_i f''_i Si_d(μ''_i; u''_i) for all d ∈ Z.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 1.3 (3), p. 11, proof p. 14 (published: Proposition 2.3 (3))
items.note: Split from item /17: proved after Parts 1–2 by factoring Si_d(ε; s) = Si_d(ε_1; s_1) Si_{<d}(ε_−; s_−) and applying Part 2 to (ε_−; s_−), (ϵ; t). Used for the operator C_{Σ,V}. If the reviewer prefers to keep Proposition 1.3 whole, merge back into /17. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The space 𝔅ℜ_w of binary relations of weight w
items.statement: 𝔅ℜ_w denotes the set of all binary relations of weight w (Definition 1.4); it is a K-vector space. An element R ∈ 𝔅ℜ_w is written R(d): Σ_i a_i Si_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i Si_{d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i) = 0 (1.5), with a_i, b_i ∈ K and all arrays of weight w; R(j) denotes the identity at d = j.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.2, p. 14 (after Definition 1.4) and (1.5), pp. 14–15 (published: Section 2.2)
items.note: Domain and target of the operators B*_{σ,v}, C_{Σ,V} and BC_{ε,q}. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The fundamental binary relation R_ε
items.statement: For ε ∈ F_q^× and D_1 = θ^q − θ ∈ A, R_ε: Si_d(ε; q) + ε^{−1} D_1 Si_{d+1}(ε, 1; 1, q − 1) = 0 for all d ∈ Z; R_ε ∈ 𝔅ℜ_q.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.2, p. 14 (published: Section 2.2); also arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.2, p. 14 (published: Section 2.2), from [36, §3.4.6] and Lemma 1.2; AMZV form in Section 4.1.2, pp. 44–45 (published: Section 5.1.2)
items.note: The paper derives it from Thakur's fundamental relation [36, §3.4.6] (Thakur, 'Relations between multizeta values for F_q[t]', IMRN 2009), a black box, in the form S_d(q) + D_1 S_{d+1}(1, q − 1) = 0, together with Lemma 1.2; R_ε is ε^d times R_1. I checked it directly: ℓ_{d+1} = ℓ_d(θ − θ^{q^{d+1}}) gives Σ_{j=0}^{d} ℓ_j^{1−q} = −ℓ_{d+1}/(D_1 ℓ_d^q) by induction on d ≥ 0, which is R_1(d); both terms vanish for d < 0. Seed of Proposition 1.6, the operator BC and Proposition 1.7; reused for AMZVs in Section 4. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The operators B*_{σ,v} and B*_{Σ,V}
items.statement: For a depth-one array (σ; v), B*_{σ,v}: 𝔅ℜ_w → 𝔅ℜ_{w+v} sends R as in (1.5) to B*_{σ,v}(R) = Si_d(σ; v) Σ_{j<d} R(j), the fixed relation 0 = Si_d(σ; v)(Σ_i a_i Si_{<d}(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i Si_{<d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i)) = Σ_i a_i Si_d(σ, ε_i; v, s_i) + Σ_i b_i Si_d(σ, ϵ_i; v, t_i) + Σ_i b_i Si_d(σϵ_{i1}, ϵ_{i−}; v + t_{i1}, t_{i−}) (the last step by (1.2)). For an array (Σ; V) = (σ_1 … σ_n; v_1 … v_n), B*_{Σ,V}(R) := B*_{σ_1,v_1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ B*_{σ_n,v_n}(R).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.2.1, p. 15 (published: Section 2.2.1)
items.note: Todd's operator B* [40] extended to ACMPLs; its iterate is described by Lemma 1.5 (item /19). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The operator C_{Σ,V}
items.statement: For an array (Σ; V) of weight v, C_{Σ,V}: 𝔅ℜ_w → 𝔅ℜ_{w+v} sends R as in (1.5) to C_{Σ,V}(R) = R(d) Si_{<d+1}(Σ; V), i.e. 0 = Σ_i a_i Si_d(ε_i; s_i) Si_d(Σ; V) + Σ_i a_i Si_d(ε_i; s_i) Si_{<d}(Σ; V) + Σ_i b_i Si_{d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i) Si_{<d+1}(Σ; V), which by Proposition 1.3 is a binary relation Σ_i c_i Si_d(μ_i; u_i) + Σ_i c'_i Si_{d+1}(μ'_i; u'_i) = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.2.2, pp. 15–16 (published: Section 2.2.2)
items.note: Todd's operator C [40] extended to ACMPLs. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The relation C_{Σ,V}(R_ε) (Proposition 1.6)
items.statement: Let (Σ; V) be an array with V = (v_1, V_−) and Σ = (σ_1, Σ_−). Then C_{Σ,V}(R_ε) is of the form Si_d(εσ_1, Σ_−; q + v_1, V_−) + Si_d(ε, Σ; q, V) + Σ_i b_i Si_{d+1}(ε, ϵ_i; 1, t_i) = 0, where b_i ∈ A are divisible by D_1 and (ϵ_i; t_i) are arrays satisfying (ϵ_i; t_i) ≤ (1; q − 1) + (Σ; V) for all i.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 1.6, p. 16 (published: Proposition 2.6)
items.note: Split from item /19. Proof checked: (1.2) gives the first two terms, and Proposition 1.3 (2) applied to Si_{<d+1}(1; q − 1) Si_{<d+1}(Σ; V) gives b_i = ε^{−1} f'_i D_1 with f'_i ∈ F_q. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The operator BC_{ε,q} and the form of BC_{ε,q}(R)
items.statement: For ε ∈ F_q^×, BC_{ε,q}: 𝔅ℜ_w → 𝔅ℜ_{w+q} sends R as in (1.5) to BC_{ε,q}(R) = B*_{ε,q}(R) − Σ_i b_i C_{ϵ_i,t_i}(R_ε). It is of the form Σ_i a_i Si_d(ε, ε_i; q, s_i) + Σ_{i,j} b_{ij} Si_{d+1}(ε, ϵ_{ij}; 1, t_{ij}) = 0, where b_{ij} ∈ K and (ϵ_{ij}; t_{ij}) are arrays with (ϵ_{ij}; t_{ij}) ≤ (1; q − 1) + (ϵ_i; t_i) for all j.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 1.2.3, pp. 16–17 (published: Section 2.2.3)
items.note: Ngo Dac's operator BC [30] extended to ACMPLs: it cancels the b-terms of B*_{ε,q}(R) against C_{ϵ_i,t_i}(R_ε). Checked. Not stated but used in Proposition 1.7: b_{ij} = −b_i ε^{−1} f'_{ij} D_1 with f'_{ij} ∈ F_q, so if the b_i lie in A (or D_1 A) so do the b_{ij}. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Decomposition of an ACMPL with Init(s) = s and last entry q (Proposition 1.7, Part 2)
items.statement: Let (ε; s) = (ε_1 … ε_k; s_1 … s_k) be an array such that Init(s) = s and s_k = q. Then Li(ε; s) = Σ_i b_i Li(ϵ'_i; t'_i) [type 2] + Σ_i c_i Li(μ_i; u_i) [type 3], where b_i, c_i ∈ A are divisible by D_1 and, for all i: (a) every array (ϵ; t) appearing on the right-hand side satisfies depth(t) ≥ depth(s) and T_k(t) ≤ T_k(s); (b) every type-2 array (ϵ'; t') satisfies t'_1 + ⋯ + t'_k < s_1 + ⋯ + s_k; (c) every type-3 array (μ; u) satisfies Init(s) ≺ Init(u).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 1.7, Part 2), pp. 17–18, proof pp. 20–21 (published: Proposition 2.7 (2))
items.note: Split from item /20. Proof (checked): apply BC_{ε_{j+1},q} ∘ ⋯ ∘ BC_{ε_{k−1},q} to R_{ε_k}, where j is maximal with s_j < q (s_0 := 0), then B*_{Σ',V'} with (Σ'; V') = (ε_1 … ε_j; s_1 … s_j), and sum over d. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Thakur: power sums S_d(s) for s ≤ q (cited)
items.statement: For 1 ≤ s ≤ q and d ≥ 0, S_d(s) = Σ_{a ∈ A_+, deg a = d} a^{−s} = 1/ℓ_d^s; consequently S_d(ε; s) = ε^d/ℓ_d^s = Si_d(ε; s) for every depth-one array (ε; s) with s ≤ q (both sides vanish for d < 0).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Lemma 1.2, p. 10, citing [36, §3.3] = D. Thakur, 'Relations between multizeta values for F_q[t]', IMRN 2009 (published: proof of Lemma 2.2); also arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Lemma 1.2, p. 10 (published: proof of Lemma 2.2), citing [36, §3.3]
items.note: Black box: the base case of the induction proving Lemma 1.2. Section number not checked against Thakur's paper. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The generating set AT_w
items.statement: For w ∈ N, AT_w is the set of ACMPLs Li(ε; s) = Li(ε_1 … ε_n; s_1 … s_n) of weight w with s_1, …, s_{n−1} ≤ q and s_n < q, that is with s ∈ J_w, and ε ∈ (F_q^×)^n arbitrary. Its elements are indexed by the arrays (ε; s) of weight w with s ∈ J_w. One puts t(w) := |AT_w|.
items.note: Split off from item 23. Reused in the proof of Theorem 1.11 (as its index set, misprinted there as AJ_w), and in §4 for AMZVs, which refers to it as 'introduced in the paragraph preceding Proposition 1.10'. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Cardinality t(w) of AT_w
items.statement: t(w) = |AT_w| satisfies t(w) = (q − 1)q^{w−1} for 1 ≤ w < q, t(q) = (q − 1)(q^{q−1} − 1), and t(w) = (q − 1)Σ_{i=1}^{q} t(w − i) for w > q.
items.note: The paper gives no proof ('one verifies that'). The recursion removes the first entry s_1 = i ∈ {1, …, q} and its q − 1 characters. Brute-force check for q ≤ 5, w ≤ 12 agrees. Split off from item 23. Used only for the comparison |AS_w| < |AT_w| in §1.4.1. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: w-admissible tuples of weight w are exactly the tuples in J_w
items.statement: A nonempty tuple s = (s_1, …, s_n) of weight w is w-admissible (Definition 1.8 with k = w) if and only if s_1, …, s_{n−1} ≤ q and s_n < q, i.e. s ∈ J_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), implicit in the proof of Proposition 1.10, p. 24 (published: Proposition 2.10)
items.note: The paper does not state this. It is the whole content of 'the result follows immediately from Proposition 1.9 in the case of k = w'. Since n ≤ w, condition 1) of Definition 1.8 says every entry is ≤ q, and condition 2) excludes s_n = q. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Block contraction of an AT-array to an AS-array
items.statement: Let (ε; s) be an array of weight w with s ∈ J_w. Write it uniquely as the concatenation of the blocks (ε_{m_i+1} … ε_{m_i+h_i−1}; q … q)(ε_{m_i+h_i}; r_i), i = 1, …, ℓ, where m_i = h_1 + ⋯ + h_{i−1}, h_i ≥ 1, h_1 + ⋯ + h_ℓ = n and 0 < r_i < q. Set ε'_i = ε_{m_i+1} ⋯ ε_{m_i+h_i} and s'_i = (h_i − 1)q + r_i. Then s' ∈ J'_w, ι(s') = s, χ(ε') = χ(ε), and Li(ε'; s') ∈ AS_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Theorem 1.11, p. 25 (published: proof of Theorem 2.11)
items.note: The map (ε; s) ↦ (ε'; s') is onto the AS-arrays but not injective ('we allow repeated elements'). It indexes the rows of the transition matrix in the proof of Theorem 1.11. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The AT-to-AS transition matrix is ±identity modulo D_1
items.statement: Let (ε; s) be an array of weight w with s ∈ J_w and (ε'; s') its block contraction. Then Li(ε'; s') = Σ a_{e,t} Li(e; t), where (e; t) runs over the arrays of weight w with t ∈ J_w, all a_{e,t} ∈ A, a_{ε,s} ≡ ±1 (mod D_1) (the sign is (−1)^{n−ℓ}), and a_{e,t} ≡ 0 (mod D_1) for (e; t) ≠ (ε; s). Consequently the square matrix indexed by the AT-arrays has determinant ≡ ±1 (mod D_1), so it is invertible over K. Hence every element of AT_w is a K-linear combination of elements of AS_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Theorem 1.11, p. 25 (published: proof of Theorem 2.11)
items.note: The core step of the strong Brown theorem. The paper prints the index set as 'AJ_w' (a misprint: AJ_w is the AS index set, E13) and asserts the congruence 'from Proposition 1.7 and Proposition 1.10' without argument (a gap, E12). The statement is true: run the algorithm of the proof of Proposition 1.9 with k = w, using Proposition 1.7 at every step with suitably chosen ε. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The Tate algebra 𝕋, its fraction field 𝕃, the ring ℰ of entire series and a(t)
items.statement: Let t be a variable independent of θ. 𝕋 is the Tate algebra in t with coefficients in ℂ_∞ (power series converging on |t|_∞ ≤ 1), equipped with the Gauss norm ‖·‖_∞, and 𝕃 is the fraction field of 𝕋. ℰ is the ring of series Σ_{n≥0} a_nt^n ∈ K̄[[t]] with lim_{n→+∞} |a_n|_∞^{1/n} = 0 and [K_∞(a_0,a_1,…) : K_∞] < ∞; every f ∈ ℰ is an entire function. For a ∈ A = F_q[θ], a(t) := a|_{θ=t} ∈ F_q[t].
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2, opening paragraphs, p. 26 (published: Section 3)
items.note: ℰ is the ring in the ABP criterion (Theorem 2.2); 𝕋 and 𝕃 are where rigid analytic trivializations live; a(t) enters (2.8) and Φ, Ψ in the proof of Theorem 2.4. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Frobenius twisting and the ring K̄[t,σ]
items.statement: For i ∈ ℤ the i-fold twisting of ℂ_∞((t)) is f = Σ_j a_jt^j ↦ f^{(i)} := Σ_j a_j^{q^i} t^j, extended to matrices with entries in ℂ_∞((t)) by twisting entry-wise. K̄[t,σ] is the non-commutative K̄[t]-algebra generated by a variable σ subject to σf = f^{(−1)}σ for all f ∈ K̄[t].
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2.1, p. 26 (published: Section 3.1)
items.note: Needed for Definition 2.1 (item 26) and for every difference equation in §§2–3. Planned: DM.8 constructs the neutral Tannakian category of rigid analytically trivial motives of Papanikolas's theorem with its analytic trivialisation matrix, built from σ-modules over K̄[t] with their Frobenius twisting.

items.name: The category ℱ, dual t-motives given by a matrix, and rigid analytic trivializations
items.statement: A morphism M → M' of effective dual t-motives is a homomorphism of left K̄[t,σ]-modules. ℱ denotes the category of effective dual t-motives, with trivial object 1. An object M of ℱ is given by Φ ∈ Mat_r(K̄[t]) if M is free of rank r over K̄[t] and σ acts on a given K̄[t]-basis of M through Φ. M is uniformizable (rigid analytically trivial) if there is Ψ ∈ GL_r(𝕋) with Ψ^{(−1)} = ΦΨ, and such a Ψ is called a rigid analytic trivialization of M.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2.1, p. 26 (published: Section 3.1)
items.note: Used in §2.2 (Ψ_{s,Q}) and throughout the proof of Theorem 2.4. Effective dual t-motives are the 'Frobenius modules' of [CPY19, CH21, Har21, KL16]. Planned: DM.8 constructs the neutral Tannakian category of rigid analytically trivial motives of Papanikolas's theorem with its analytic trivialisation matrix, built from σ-modules over K̄[t] with their Frobenius twisting.

items.name: The function Ω and the Carlitz period π̃
items.statement: π̃ is a fixed fundamental period of the Carlitz module. Fix a (q−1)-st root of −θ and set Ω(t) := (−θ)^{−q/(q−1)} Π_{i≥1}(1 − t/θ^{q^i}) ∈ 𝕋^×, so that Ω^{(−1)} = (t−θ)Ω and 1/Ω(θ) = π̃. Ω is entire, and its zeros are simple and are exactly the points t = θ^{q^k}, k ∈ ℕ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2.2.1, p. 27 (published: Section 3.2.1); the simple zeros at θ^{q^k} are used on pp. 32–33
items.note: Checked: Ω^{(−1)} = (−θ)^{−1/(q−1)}(1 − t/θ)Π_{i≥1}(1 − t/θ^{q^i}) = (t−θ)Ω. The normalisation 1/Ω(θ) = π̃ holds for a suitable choice of the root (π̃ is determined only up to F_q^×), as [CPY19, §2.3] says explicitly. The coefficients of Ω are algebraic over K (recursion from Ω^{(−1)} = (t−θ)Ω), so Ω ∈ ℰ, which the ABP criterion needs in the proof of Theorem 2.4. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Chang's series 𝔏(s;Q) is entire (cited)
items.statement: If s ∈ ℕ^r and Q ∈ K̄[t]^r satisfy Condition (2.1), then the series 𝔏(s;Q) of (2.2) belongs to ℰ.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2.2.1, p. 27 (published: Section 3.2.1), quoting [Cha14, Lemma 5.3.1]
items.note: A black box from Chang (Compositio Math. 150 (2014)). I checked that Lemma 5.3.1 there is this statement under the same hypothesis. Chang deduces it from the ABP result [ABP04, Prop. 3.1.1] that 𝕋-solutions of such difference equations are entire. Needed so that the ABP criterion applies to the vector ψ̃ in the proof of Theorem 2.4. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The Frobenius property (2.3) of 𝔏(s;Q) (cited)
items.statement: For s ∈ ℕ^r and Q ∈ K̄[t]^r satisfying Condition (2.1) and every j ∈ ℤ^{≥0}, 𝔏(s;Q)(θ^{q^j}) = (𝔏(s;Q)(θ))^{q^j}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Eq. (2.3), p. 27 (published: Eq. (3.3)), quoting [Cha14, Lemma 5.3.5] and [CPY19, Proposition 2.3.3]
items.note: Called 'crucial' by the authors; the proof of Theorem 2.4 uses it for prefixes and tails of the s_i (pp. 32–33). Chang's Lemma 5.3.5 is for constant Q (algebraic points); CPY19, Prop. 2.3.3 is the stated general form. Proof idea: the terms with i_r < j vanish at θ^{q^j} because Ω^{(i)} vanishes at θ^{q^m} for m > i, and the rest is 𝔏^{(j)}. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Carlitz factorials and the Anderson–Thakur polynomials H_n
items.statement: For k ≥ 0, [k] := θ^{q^k} − θ and D_k := Π_{ℓ=1}^k [ℓ]^{q^{k−ℓ}}. For n ∈ ℕ write n − 1 = Σ_{j≥0} n_jq^j with 0 ≤ n_j ≤ q−1 and put Γ_n := Π_{j≥0} D_j^{n_j}. Set γ_0(t) := 1 and γ_j(t) := Π_{ℓ=1}^j (θ^{q^j} − t^{q^ℓ}) for j ≥ 1. The Anderson–Thakur polynomials α_n(t) ∈ A[t] are defined by Σ_{n≥1} (α_n(t)/Γ_n) x^n := x(1 − Σ_{j≥0} (γ_j(t)/D_j) x^{q^j})^{−1}, and H_n(t) := α_n(t)|_{t=θ, θ=t} (θ and t switched).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2.2.2, p. 28 (published: Section 3.2.2), after [AT90] and [AT09]
items.note: The γ_j(t) here are unrelated to the roots γ_i of ε_i. With this indexing, the paper's H_n is the H_{n−1} of [AT90] and [Cha14, §5.5]. That matches the bound (2.4) with (n−1) and the formula (2.5). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The θ-degree bound (2.4) for H_n (cited)
items.statement: For n ∈ ℕ, deg_θ H_n ≤ (n−1)q/(q−1) < nq/(q−1); consequently ‖H_n‖_∞ < |θ|_∞^{nq/(q−1)}.
items.note: Gives Condition (2.1) for Q_{s,ε} = (γ_iH_{s_i}), and indeed the termwise bound ‖Q_i‖ < |θ|^{qs_i/(q−1)}. Consistent with the Anderson–Thakur theorem quoted in [Cha14, §5.5] (bound nq/(q−1) for Chang's H_n = the paper's H_{n+1}). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Dual t-motives attached to AMZVs and the series 𝔏(s;ε)
items.statement: Let s = (s_1,…,s_r) ∈ ℕ^r and ε = (ε_1,…,ε_r) ∈ (F_q^×)^r. For each 1 ≤ i ≤ r fix a (q−1)-th root γ_i ∈ F̄_q of ε_i and set Q_{s_i,ε_i} := γ_iH_{s_i}, Q_{s,ε} := (Q_{s_1,ε_1},…,Q_{s_r,ε_r}) and 𝔏(s;ε) := 𝔏(s;Q_{s,ε}). By (2.4), Q_{s,ε} satisfies Condition (2.1). This gives the dual t-motives M_{s,ε} := M_{s,Q_{s,ε}} and M'_{s,ε} := M'_{s,Q_{s,ε}}, with matrices and rigid analytic trivializations (Φ_{s,ε},Ψ_{s,ε}) and (Φ'_{s,ε},Ψ'_{s,ε}).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2.2.2, pp. 28–29 (published: Section 3.2.2), after [AT09]
items.note: The main line (Theorems A and B) goes through ACMPLs and does not use it. It is used where Theorem 2.4 is applied directly to AMZVs in the sketch of the proof of Proposition 4.13, p. 58 (published 5.13). Split out of the bundled item 28 ('Section 2.2'). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Period interpretation of AMZVs (2.5) and non-vanishing (cited)
items.statement: For s ∈ ℕ^r and ε ∈ (F_q^×)^r as above, 𝔏(s;ε)(θ) = γ_1⋯γ_rΓ_{s_1}⋯Γ_{s_r}ζ_A(ε;s)/π̃^{w(s)}. Since ζ_A(ε;s) ≠ 0, also 𝔏(s;ε)(θ) ≠ 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Eq. (2.5), p. 29 (published: Eq. (3.5)), quoting [CH21, Proposition 2.12] and, for ζ_A(ε;s) ≠ 0, [Har21, Theorem 2.1] after Thakur
items.note: For ε = (1,…,1) this is Chang's formula in [Cha14, §5.5], Γ_{s_1}⋯Γ_{s_r}ζ_A(s) = π̃^w𝔏(s)(θ), after [AT09]. The factor γ_1⋯γ_r comes from γ^{q^d} = ε^dγ. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Dual t-motives attached to ACMPLs and the series 𝔏i(s;ε)
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℕ^r and ε ∈ (F_q^×)^r, with the fixed (q−1)-th roots γ_i of ε_i. Set Q'_{s_i,ε_i} := γ_i, Q'_{s,ε} := (γ_1,…,γ_r) and (2.6) 𝔏i(s;ε) := 𝔏(s;Q'_{s,ε}) = Σ_{i_1>⋯>i_r≥0} (γ_rΩ^{s_r})^{(i_r)} ⋯ (γ_1Ω^{s_1})^{(i_1)}. The printed formula has γ_{i_r}, …, γ_{i_1}; see the source issue. This defines the dual t-motives N_{s,ε} := M_{s,Q'_{s,ε}} and N'_{s,ε} := M'_{s,Q'_{s,ε}} attached to (s,ε).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 2.2.3, Eq. (2.6), p. 29 (published: Section 3.2.3, Eq. (3.6))
items.note: The object of §3: Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 apply Theorem 2.4 to 𝔏i, with Q_{ij} = γ_{ij} ∈ F̄_q^×. The constants γ_i have norm 1, so (2.1) holds for every sub-tuple. Split out of the bundled item 28. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Period interpretation of ACMPLs (2.7) (cited)
items.statement: For s ∈ ℕ^r and ε ∈ (F_q^×)^r, 𝔏i(s;ε)(θ) = γ_1⋯γ_r Li(ε;s)/π̃^{w(s)}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Eq. (2.7), p. 29 (published: Eq. (3.7)), quoting [Cha14, Lemma 5.3.5] and [CPY19, Prop. 2.3.3]
items.note: Checked directly: Ω^{(i)}(θ) = 1/(π̃ℓ_i) with ℓ_i = Π_{k=1}^i(θ − θ^{q^k}), and γ^{q^i} = ε^iγ, so the series at θ is γ_1⋯γ_r Σ ε_1^{i_1}⋯ε_r^{i_r}/(π̃^wℓ_{i_1}^{s_1}⋯ℓ_{i_r}^{s_r}). This matches item 5's definition of Li(ε;s). Used in Lemma 3.2 and in the proof of Theorem 3.4. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.5: f_∅ and the comparison with [ND21, Theorem B]
items.statement: 1) (LW) stands for Lower Weights and (LD) for Linear Dependence. 2) With the notation of Theorem 2.4, f_∅ = Σ_i a_i(t)𝔏(s_i;Q_i). 3) (printed '2)') Theorem 2.4 improves [ND21, Theorem B] in two directions. It removes the restriction to Anderson–Thakur polynomials and tuples s_i, and it allows an additional term a, which is crucial in the sequel. In the MZV case, [ND21, Theorem B] investigates linear relations between MZVs of weight w, while Theorem 2.4 investigates linear relations between MZVs of weight w and π̃^w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Remark 2.5, p. 30 (published: Remark 3.5)
items.note: Split out of the bundled item 30 ('Theorem 2.4 with Remark 2.5'). Part 2) is (2.8) with k = 0. The printed numbering is 1), 2), 2); see the source issue. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Denominators of morphisms of Frobenius modules lie in F_q[t] (cited)
items.statement: For i = 1, 2 let M_i be an effective dual t-motive given by Φ_i ∈ Mat_{r_i}(K̄[t]) with det Φ_i = c_i(t−θ)^{s_i}, c_i ∈ K̄^×, s_i ≥ 0. If F ∈ Mat_{r_1×r_2}(K̄(t)) satisfies F^{(−1)}Φ_2 = Φ_1F (that is, F represents a K̄(t)[σ]-linear map K̄(t)⊗M_1 → K̄(t)⊗M_2), then the common denominator of the entries of F lies in F_q[t].
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Theorem 2.4, p. 33 (published: proof of Theorem 3.4), quoting [CPY19, Prop. 2.2.1]
items.note: The paper applies it with F = (1 0 0; 0 Id 0; g_0/g (g_{t,Q}/g) 1), Φ_2 = Φ̃ and Φ_1 = diag(1, Φ', 1), which gives b ∈ F_q[t]∖{0}. I checked the statement against CPY19's source. CPY19 prints F ∈ Mat(K̄[t]), a slip for K̄(t), as its proof shows. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Rigid analytic trivializations are unique up to GL(F_q(t)) (cited)
items.statement: Let Φ ∈ Mat_r(K̄[t]) ∩ GL_r(K̄(t)) and let Ψ ∈ GL_r(𝕋) satisfy Ψ^{(−1)} = ΦΨ. If X ∈ GL_r(𝕃) also satisfies X^{(−1)} = ΦX, then X = ΨN for some N ∈ GL_r(F_q(t)).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Theorem 2.4, p. 33 (published: proof of Theorem 3.4), quoting [Pap08, §4.1.6]
items.note: Applied with Φ = diag(Φ', 1), Ψ = diag(Ψ', 1) and X = (Id 0; δ 1)(Ψ' 0; bf 1). Then N = (Id 0; ν 1) automatically, giving (2.13) δΨ' + bf = ν. It rests on the fact that the elements of 𝕃 fixed by twisting are F_q(t). The step ν ∈ F_q(t) ∩ 𝕋 = F_q[t] is elementary. Planned: DM.8 constructs the neutral Tannakian category of rigid analytically trivial motives of Papanikolas's theorem with its analytic trivialisation matrix, built from σ-modules over K̄[t] with their Frobenius twisting.

items.name: The transcendence theorem needs the strong Brown theorem
items.statement: Although Theorem 3.4 is a purely transcendental result, its proof needs the full strength of the algebraic theory for ACMPLs, i.e. Theorem 1.11 (AS_w generates AL_w), in its last step: to exhibit a relation between π̃^w and ACMPLs in AS_w whose coefficient of π̃^w is non-zero.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Remark 3.5, p. 36 (published: Remark 4.5)
items.note: Split from the bundle PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/34. A methodological remark rather than a mathematical statement; it records a real dependency (the ABP analysis requires q ∤ s_i, so the weak Brown theorem, whose generators AT_w allow s_i = q, would not suffice). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: No constant term when q − 1 does not divide the weight
items.statement: If q − 1 ∤ w, then π̃^w ∉ F̄_q((1/θ)); consequently every relation a + Σ_i a_i 𝔏𝔦(s_i; ε_i)(θ) = 0 with a, a_i ∈ K and s_i ∈ J'_w (of weight w) has a = 0.
items.note: Unnumbered claim used in the base case w = 1 and in Case 1 of the proof of Theorem 3.4. Proof: by (2.7), a π̃^w = −Σ_i a_i γ_{i1}⋯γ_{iℓ_i} Li(ε_i; s_i) lies in F_{q^N}((1/θ)), whose non-zero elements have integral valuation, while v_∞(π̃^w) = −qw/(q − 1) ∉ Z. The companion fact used implicitly in the character split (see notes) is that π̃^w ∈ K_∞ when q − 1 | w. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Carlitz's evaluation of ζ_A(q − 1)
items.statement: Li(q − 1) = ζ_A(q − 1) = −D_1^{−1} π̃^{q−1}, where D_1 = θ^q − θ. In particular, for q = 2, Li(1) = ζ_A(1) = −D_1^{−1} π̃.
items.note: Used as a black box (no reference given at that point) in the base case q = 2, w = 1 and in the final step of the proof of Theorem 3.4, where Li(q − 1)^m = (−D_1)^{−m} π̃^{(q−1)m}. The equality Li(q − 1) = ζ_A(q − 1) is Lemma 1.2 (item 16); the evaluation of ζ_A(q − 1) is Carlitz's (with the paper's normalisation of π̃, the leading terms agree: −D_1^{−1}(−θ)^q ≈ 1). Planned: DM.6 requires the Carlitz module to recover its explicit zeta value and period normalisation, which is Carlitz's evaluation.

items.name: The σ-difference system extracted from the ABP criterion
items.statement: Under the hypotheses (LW) and (LD) of Theorem 2.4 (a, a_i ∈ A), there exist b ∈ F_q[t] ∖ {0}, δ_0 ∈ K̄[t] with δ_0^{(−1)} = δ_0, and δ = (δ_{t;Q})_{(t;Q) ∈ I} ∈ Mat_{1×|I|}(K̄[t]) such that [[Id, 0], [δ, 1]]^{(−1)} [[Φ', 0], [b v, 1]] = [[Φ', 0], [0, 1]] [[Id, 0], [δ, 1]], i.e. δ = δ^{(−1)} Φ' + b v. Here Φ' ∈ Mat_{|I|}(K̄[t]) has Φ'_{∅,∅} = (t − θ)^w, Φ'_{(t;Q),(t;Q)} = (t − θ)^{w − w(t)}, and Φ'_{(t;Q),(t';Q')} = Q_{ij}^{(−1)} (t − θ)^{w − w(t')} when (t; Q) = (s_{i1}, …, s_{ij}; Q_{i1}, …, Q_{ij}) and (t'; Q') = (s_{i1}, …, s_{i(j−1)}; Q_{i1}, …, Q_{i(j−1)}), all other entries 0; and v_{t;Q} = Σ_i a_i(t) Q_{iℓ_i}^{(−1)} (t − θ)^{w − w(t)}, the sum over the i with (t; Q) = (s_{i1}, …, s_{i(ℓ_i−1)}; Q_{i1}, …, Q_{i(ℓ_i−1)}).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Theorem 2.4, Eq. (2.12), p. 33 (published: proof of Theorem 3.4, Eq. (3.12))
items.note: An intermediate result of the proof of Theorem 2.4 (D's page range), not contained in its statement (which only concludes f_{t;Q}(θ) ∈ K), but used as a black box in the proof of Theorem 3.4 ('Now we want to solve (2.12)', p. 37; rewritten as (3.4)–(3.5) on p. 38 with δ_{s_i;ε_i} := a_i(t) and b normalised to 1 by rescaling the relation by b(θ)). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Harada's depth-one product formula for alternating power sums
items.statement: For s, t ∈ N, ε, ϵ ∈ F_q^× and all d ∈ Z: S_d(ε; s) S_d(ϵ; t) = S_d(εϵ; s + t) + Σ_i Δ^i_{s,t} S_d((εϵ, 1); (s + t − i, i)), where Δ^i_{s,t} = (−1)^{s−1} C(i − 1, s − 1) + (−1)^{t−1} C(i − 1, t − 1) if q − 1 | i and 0 < i < s + t, and Δ^i_{s,t} = 0 otherwise.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), §4.1.1, Eqs. (4.1)–(4.2), pp. 43–44 (published: §5.1.1, Eqs. (5.1)–(5.2)); cited from Harada [21], via Chen's formula [13]; also arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 4.1.1, equations (4.1)–(4.2), pp. 43–44 (published: Section 5.1.1, (5.1)–(5.2)); cited from Chen [13] and Harada [21]
items.note: Black box used for Remark 4.1 and in the proof of Proposition 4.5. It is Chen's formula for S_d(s)S_d(t) multiplied by (εϵ)^d, using S_d(ε; s) = ε^d S_d(s) and S_d((εϵ, 1); (s+t−i, i)) = (εϵ)^d S_d(s+t−i, i). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Binary and fixed relations between AMZV power sums
items.statement: A binary relation is a K-linear combination of the form Σ_i a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i S_{d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i) = 0 holding for all d ∈ Z, where a_i, b_i ∈ K and the arrays (ε_i; s_i), (ϵ_i; t_i) all have the same weight. A binary relation is a fixed relation if b_i = 0 for all i. ℜ_w denotes the set of binary relations of weight w; a relation R ∈ ℜ_w is written R(d): Σ_i a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i S_{d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i) = 0 (4.3).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Definition 4.3 and Eq. (4.3), pp. 44–45 (published: Definition 5.3 and Eq. (5.3))
items.note: Split from the bundle PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/37; the AMZV analogue of Definition 1.4 (item 18), with S_d in place of 𝔖_d. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The fundamental binary relation R_ε for AMZV power sums
items.statement: For ε ∈ F_q^×, R_ε: S_d(ε; q) + ε^{−1} D_1 S_{d+1}((ε, 1); (1, q − 1)) = 0 for all d ∈ Z, where D_1 = θ^q − θ; it is a binary relation of weight q.
items.note: Obtained from the ACMPL relation R_ε of §1.2 and Lemma 1.2 (S_d = 𝔖_d for arrays with all entries ≤ q; here (q) and (1, q − 1)). Used in Proposition 4.5 and the operators BC. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The operators B* on AMZV binary relations
items.statement: For a depth-one array (σ; v), B*_{σ,v}: ℜ_w → ℜ_{w+v} sends R ∈ ℜ_w as in (4.3) to the fixed relation S_d(σ; v) Σ_{j<d} R(j) = 0, i.e. S_d(σ; v)(Σ_i a_i S_{<d}(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i S_{<d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i)) = 0, which equals Σ_i a_i S_d((σ, ε_i); (v, s_i)) + Σ_i b_i S_d((σ, ϵ_i); (v, t_i)) + Σ_i b_i Σ_j f_{i,j} S_d(μ_{i,j}; u_{i,j}) = 0, where S_d(σ; v) S_d(ϵ_i; t_i) = Σ_j f_{i,j} S_d(μ_{i,j}; u_{i,j}) by Proposition 4.2(1). For an array (Σ; V) = (σ_1 … σ_n; v_1 … v_n), B*_{Σ,V} := B*_{σ_1,v_1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ B*_{σ_n,v_n}.
items.note: Unnumbered construction on which Lemma 4.4 is stated; verified (Σ_{j<d} S_{j+1} = S_{<d+1} = S_{<d} + S_d and S_d(σ; v) S_{<d}(ε; s) = S_d((σ, ε); (v, s))). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The operators C on AMZV binary relations
items.statement: For an array (Σ; V) of weight v, C_{Σ,V}: ℜ_w → ℜ_{w+v} sends R ∈ ℜ_w as in (4.3) to the binary relation R(d) S_{<d+1}(Σ; V) = 0, i.e. Σ_i a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) S_d(Σ; V) + Σ_i a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) S_{<d}(Σ; V) + Σ_i b_i S_{d+1}(ϵ_i; t_i) S_{<d+1}(Σ; V) = 0, which by Proposition 4.2 has the form Σ_i f_i S_d(μ_i; u_i) + Σ_i f'_i S_{d+1}(μ'_i; u'_i) = 0.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), §4.1.2, p. 46 (published: §5.1.2); also arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 4.1.2, definition of the operators 𝒞, p. 46 (published: Section 5.1.2)
items.note: Needed to state Proposition 4.5 (split from item 38). On p. 46, i.e. in another reading's page range: possible overlap. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The operators BC on AMZV binary relations
items.statement: For ε ∈ F_q^×, BC_{ε,q}: ℜ_w → ℜ_{w+q} sends R ∈ ℜ_w as in (4.3) to BC_{ε,q}(R) = B*_{ε,q}(R) − Σ_i b_i C_{ϵ_i,t_i}(R_ε); by Proposition 4.2 it has the form Σ_i a_i S_d((ε, ε_i); (q, s_i)) + Σ_{i,j} b_{ij} S_{d+1}((ε, ϵ_{ij}); (1, t_{ij})) = 0 with b_{ij} ∈ K and (ϵ_{ij}; t_{ij}) ≤ (1; q − 1) + (ϵ_i; t_i) for all j.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), §4.1.2, p. 47 (published: §5.1.2); also arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Section 4.1.2, definition of the operators 𝓑𝒞, p. 47 (published: Section 5.1.2)
items.note: Used in the proof of Proposition 4.6 (split from item 38). In another reading's page range: possible overlap. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The form of C_{Σ,V}(R_ε) for AMZVs
items.statement: Let (Σ; V) be an array with V = (v_1, V_−) and Σ = (σ_1, Σ_−), and ε ∈ F_q^×. Then C_{Σ,V}(R_ε) is of the form S_d((εσ_1, Σ_−); (q + v_1, V_−)) + Σ_i a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_i b_i S_{d+1}((ε, ϵ_i); (1, t_i)) = 0, where a_i, b_i ∈ K and the arrays satisfy (ε_i; s_i) ≤ (ε; q) + (Σ; V) and s_{i1} < q + v_1 for all i, and (ϵ_i; t_i) ≤ (1; q − 1) + (Σ; V) for all i.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.5, p. 46 (published: Proposition 5.5); proof pp. 46–47
items.note: Split from the bundle PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/38. Checked: the leading term comes from (4.1) applied to S_d(ε; q) S_d(σ_1; v_1); the Δ-terms have first entry q + v_1 − i < q + v_1 and S_d(ε; q) S_{<d}(Σ; V) = S_d((ε, Σ); (q, V)) has first entry q < q + v_1; the b-terms come from Proposition 4.2(2) applied to S_{<d+1}(1; q − 1) S_{<d+1}(Σ; V). Unlike Proposition 1.6 (item 19), the coefficients are only claimed to lie in K. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Decomposition of an AMZV with a large entry
items.statement: Let (ε; s) = (ε_1 … ε_n; s_1 … s_n) be an array with Init(s) = (s_1, …, s_{k−1}) for some 1 ≤ k ≤ n. Then ζ_A(ε; s) = Σ_i a_i ζ_A(ε'_i; s'_i) + Σ_i b_i ζ_A(ϵ'_i; t'_i) + Σ_i c_i ζ_A(μ_i; u_i) (terms of type 1, 2 and 3), with a_i, b_i, c_i ∈ K, such that: every array (ϵ; t) on the right-hand side has depth(t) ≥ depth(s) and T_k(t) ≤ T_k(s); every array (ε'; s') of type 1 satisfies Init(s) ≼ Init(s') and s'_k < s_k; every array (ϵ'; t') of type 2 satisfies t'_1 + ⋯ + t'_ℓ < s_1 + ⋯ + s_ℓ for all k ≤ ℓ ≤ n; every array (μ; u) of type 3 satisfies Init(s) ≺ Init(u).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.6(1), pp. 47–48 (published: Proposition 5.6(1)); proof pp. 48–50
items.note: Split from the bundle PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/38; the two parts are proved separately. AMZV analogue of Proposition 1.7(1) (item 20), without the D_1-divisibility of the coefficients. Proof in another reading's page range (not audited here). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Decomposition of an AMZV whose initial tuple ends in q
items.statement: Let (ε; s) = (ε_1 … ε_k; s_1 … s_k) be an array with Init(s) = s and s_k = q. Then ζ_A(ε; s) = Σ_i b_i ζ_A(ϵ'_i; t'_i) + Σ_i c_i ζ_A(μ_i; u_i) (terms of type 2 and 3), with b_i, c_i ∈ K, such that: every array (ϵ; t) on the right-hand side has depth(t) ≥ depth(s) and T_k(t) ≤ T_k(s); every array (ϵ'; t') of type 2 satisfies t'_1 + ⋯ + t'_k < s_1 + ⋯ + s_k; every array (μ; u) of type 3 satisfies Init(s) ≺ Init(u).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.6(2), p. 48 (published: Proposition 5.6(2)); proof pp. 50–52
items.note: Split from the bundle PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/38. Its proof uses Lemma 4.4 (with v_n + t_{i1} = s_j + 1 ≤ q). Proof in another reading's page range (not audited here). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Reduction of AMZVs to k-admissible arrays
items.statement: For all k ∈ N and all arrays (ε; s), ζ_A(ε; s) can be expressed as a K-linear combination of AMZVs ζ_A(ϵ; t) of the same weight such that t is k-admissible.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Proposition 4.7, p. 52 (published: Proposition 5.7); proof pp. 52–53
items.note: Split from the bundle PAPER-IM-KIM-LE-ETAL-24/38; k-admissible is Definition 1.8 (item 21). With k = w it gives Proposition 4.8 (item 39). Proof in another reading's page range (not audited here). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Trivial-character (CMPL) specialisation of the algebraic theory: CMPLs lie in Z_w
items.statement: All the relations of §1 hold for CMPLs, i.e. for arrays with trivial characters, 𝔖_d(s) = 𝔖_d(1, …, 1; s) and Li(s) = Li(1, …, 1; s). This covers (1.1), Proposition 1.3, R_1, the operators 𝓑*, 𝒞, 𝓑𝒞 and Propositions 1.6–1.10. Consequently every CMPL Li(s) of weight w is a K-linear combination of the Li(t) = ζ_A(t) with t ∈ J_w. In particular the CMPLs of weight w lie in Z_w.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Proposition 4.10, pp. 54–55 (published: proof of Proposition 5.10); cf. the sentence after Proposition 1.3, p. 14
items.note: Asserted without proof in the proof of Proposition 4.10, which then attributes S_w ⊂ Z_w to Theorem 4.9 (see source issue). The claim is true: products of power sums, R_1 and the three operators only multiply the characters of the input arrays, so trivial characters stay trivial. The paper makes the same restriction after Proposition 1.3 to get that ℒ is a K-algebra. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The Hoffman index sets have d(w) elements
items.statement: For every w ∈ N, two sets have d(w) elements each: the set J_w of tuples of weight w with s_1, …, s_{n−1} ≤ q and s_n < q, and the set J'_w of tuples of weight w with q ∤ s_i for all i. Hence |T_w| = d(w), and the set S_w of CMPLs Li(s), s ∈ J'_w, has |S_w| = d(w).
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Proposition 4.10, p. 55 ('by §1.4.1, |S_w| = d(w)'), with the bijection ι: J'_w → J_w of §1.4.1, p. 24 (published: proof of Proposition 5.10 and §2.4.1)
items.note: Used for the lower bound in Proposition 4.10 and for the basis part of Theorem B. §1.4.1 gives only |J'_w| = |J_w|. The count |J_w| = d(w) is never proved or stated in the paper; it is implicit in the compatibility of Conjectures 0.6 and 0.7. It is elementary: j(w) = Σ_{r=1}^{q−1} c(w − r), where c(m) counts compositions of m with parts ≤ q, satisfies the recurrence of d(w). Checked numerically for q ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5, 7} and w ≤ 3q − 2. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 4.12: the ad hoc upper bound reaches w = 2q − 1 but not w = 2q
items.statement: The condition w ≤ 2q − 2 is essential in the proof of Proposition 4.11: it significantly simplifies the expression of 𝓑*_{ε,U}𝒞_{λ,W}(R_ε), reducing it to (4.14). For w = 2q − 1 the situation is more complicated, but the authors can still prove Proposition 4.11, i.e. dim_K AZ_{2q−1} ≤ s(2q − 1). They are not able to extend it to w = 2q.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), Remark 4.12, p. 57 (published: Remark 5.12)
items.note: Split from item 42. No argument for w = 2q − 1 is given in the paper (details are in [25]). The bound itself also follows from Theorem A. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The sets I'_w and AT'_w of Proposition 4.13
items.statement: For 1 ≤ w ≤ 3q − 2, I'_w is the following set of tuples s = (s_1, …, s_r) of weight w. (1) For w ≤ 2q − 2: s_i ≠ q for all i. (2) For 2q − 1 ≤ w ≤ 3q − 3: either s_i ∉ {q, 2q − 1, 2q} for all i, or there is a unique 1 ≤ i < r with (s_i, s_{i+1}) = (q − 1, q). (3) For w = 3q − 2 and q > 2: either s_i ∉ {q, 2q − 1, 2q, 3q − 2} for all i; or there is a unique 1 ≤ i < r with (s_i, s_{i+1}) ∈ {(q − 1, q), (2q − 2, q)} but s ≠ (q − 1, q − 1, q); or s = (q − 1, 2q − 1). (4) For q = 2 and w = 4: I'_4 = {(2, 1, 1), (1, 2, 1), (1, 3)}. Then AT'_w := {ζ_A(ϵ; s) : s ∈ I'_w, ϵ_i = 1 whenever s_i ∈ {q, 2q − 1}}.
items.locator: arXiv:2205.07165v2 (10 June 2024), proof of Proposition 4.13, p. 57 (published: proof of Proposition 5.13)
items.note: The paper claims |AT'_w| = s(w) only for w ≤ 3q − 3 and for (q, w) = (2, 4). This is checked numerically for q ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5, 7}. It also claims a prefix property: if ζ_A(ϵ; s) ∈ AT'_w with w ≤ 3q − 3, then deleting the last entry gives an element of AT'_{w−s_r}; this is checked by hand. The w = 3q − 2, q > 2 clause is never used. As literally defined it gives |AT'_{3q−2}| = s(3q − 2) − (q − 1)(q − 2) for q = 3, 4, 5, 7, consistent with Proposition 4.13 excluding that case. items.statement: Let either w ≤ 3q − 3, or w = 3q − 2 and q = 2. Then dim_K AZ_w ≥ s(w).

items.note: Split from item 42. The proof is only an outline. It uses |AT'_w| = s(w), the prefix property of AT'_w, and Theorem 2.4 applied inductively on w, with the resulting σ-linear system shown to have no non-trivial solution 'by direct but complicated calculations'. Details are deferred to [25] (Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham, hal-04240841, published in Acta Math. Vietnam. 2024). items.name: Remark 4.14: Lara Rodríguez–Thakur zeta-like relations explain AT'_w
items.statement: 1) The MZVs ζ_A(1, 2q − 2) and ζ_A(2q − 1) are linearly dependent over K, and so are ζ_A(1, 3q − 3) and ζ_A(3q − 2), by [27, Theorem 3.1].
